en: to grow fierce; to grow intense; to grow strong

examples.ko: 고객 항의가 거세지자 회사는 가격 인상 철회를 바로 발표했어요.
examples.en: When customer complaints grew fierce, the company immediately announced it was withdrawing the price hike.
As night falls, the wind keeps getting stronger.

examples.ko: 어제 저녁에 비가 거세져서 우산이 소용없었어요.
examples.en: The rain got heavy last evening, so my umbrella was useless.

examples.ko: 파도가 오후에 더 거세질 거라서 바다에 들어가지 마세요.
examples.en: The waves will get rougher this afternoon, so please don't go into the sea.
The voices of opposition are getting louder and fiercer.

examples.ko: 이 강은 장마철에 물살이 갑자기 거세졌어요.
examples.en: The current of this river suddenly became fierce during the rainy season.

explain: 바람, 비, 파도, 물살처럼 자연의 힘이나 항의, 반대, 비난 같은 기세가 세지고 사나워질 때 써요. 단순히 '강해지다'보다 거칠고 격한 느낌이 있어요. 반대 느낌으로는 '약해지다'나 '잦아들다'를 써요.

phrases.en: The wind is blowing fiercely outside.
phrases.nuance_ko: '거세게'를 붙여 바람이 세고 사납다는 느낌을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 거세게 gives a feeling of strong, rough wind.

phrases.en: Voices opposing the construction have grown fierce.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람들의 반대나 항의가 점점 격해질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when opposition or protest becomes more intense.

phrases.example: 거센 파도 때문에 배가 출발하지 못했어요.
phrases.en: The ship couldn't leave because of the rough waves.
phrases.nuance_ko: '거세다'를 '-ㄴ' 형태로 바꿔 명사 앞에 쓴 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective 거세다 in its modifier form placed before a noun.

explain_en: It is used when natural forces like wind, rain, waves and currents, or momentum like protests, opposition and criticism, become stronger and rougher. It feels harsher and more intense than plain '강해지다'. The opposite feel is '약해지다' or '잦아들다'.

examples.en: The police raided the criminal's house at dawn.
The soldiers plan to launch a surprise attack on the enemy base.

examples.ko: 갑자기 비바람이 마을을 급습해서 다들 놀랐어요.
examples.en: A sudden storm hit the village and everyone was shocked.
The lion pounced on the resting deer.

examples.ko: 세무서에서 그 가게를 급습해 장부를 가져갔어요.
examples.en: The tax office raided the shop and took the account books.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 경찰이 불법 도박장을 급습했다고 해요.
examples.en: The news says the police raided an illegal gambling den.

explain: 예고 없이 갑자기 쳐들어가거나 덮친다는 점에서 '습격하다'와 비슷한데, 급습은 '갑작스러움'이 중심이에요. 경찰·군대 뉴스에서 많이 쓰고, 날씨나 병이 갑자기 닥칠 때도 비유로 써요.

phrases.en: The police raided that shop last night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형으로, 뉴스에서 갑자기 덮친 일을 전할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past form, often used in news about a sudden raid.

phrases.en: The village was attacked suddenly in the middle of the night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 공격받은 쪽에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of those who were suddenly attacked.

phrases.en: They say thieves attacked the house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 뜻이지만 '갑작스러움'보다 공격 자체에 더 무게가 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning, but focuses more on the attack than on the suddenness.

explain_en: It means striking suddenly without warning, close to 습격하다 but with the stress on suddenness. Common in police and military news, and used figuratively for weather or illness that hits all at once.

examples.en: Wild geese are flying across the autumn sky.
The geese are flying in a V shape.
When winter comes, wild geese come to Korea.
We watched wild geese by the lake.

examples.ko: 결혼식에서 기러기 인형을 전해 주는 풍습이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a custom of presenting a wooden goose at a wedding.
Wild geese are birds that migrate far.

explain: 기러기는 가을에 와서 봄에 떠나는 철새예요. 한국에서는 '기러기 아빠'가 아이 교육을 위해 아내와 아이를 외국에 보내고 혼자 사는 아버지를 가리키는 표현이기도 해요. 오리나 거위와는 다른 새예요.

phrases.example: 옆집 아저씨는 기러기 아빠로 혼자 살고 계세요.
phrases.en: The man next door lives alone as a 'goose father'.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아이 교육을 위해 가족을 외국에 보내고 혼자 한국에 남아 일하는 아버지를 말해요. 철새처럼 가족을 만나러 오가는 모습에서 나온 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A father who stays in Korea to work while his family lives abroad for the children's schooling, flying out to see them like a migratory bird.

explain_en: 기러기 is a migratory bird that arrives in autumn and leaves in spring. In Korea, '기러기 아빠' also means a father who lives alone while his wife and children stay abroad for the children's education. It is a different bird from ducks and domestic geese.

examples.ko: 비가 오면 도랑에 물이 가득 차요.
examples.en: When it rains, the ditch fills with water.
The kids caught frogs in the ditch.
My shoes got wet while crossing the ditch.
The stream in front of the village is clear and cool.

examples.ko: 아버지가 도랑 옆에 작은 길을 만들었어요.
examples.en: My father made a small path beside the ditch.

examples.ko: 낙엽 때문에 도랑이 막혀서 물이 넘쳤어요.
examples.en: Fallen leaves blocked the ditch and the water overflowed.

explain: '강'과 '개울'보다 작고, '도랑'은 사람이 물을 대거나 빼려고 판 좁은 물길일 때가 많아요. 도시에서는 '하수구'를 더 흔하게 쓰고, '도랑'은 시골 이야기에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 도랑 치고 가재 잡는다더니, 청소하다가 잃어버린 반지도 찾았어요.
phrases.en: Clean the ditch and catch a crayfish too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 가지 일을 하다가 뜻밖에 다른 이득까지 얻을 때 쓰는 속담이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb used when doing one task brings an unexpected extra benefit.
phrases.en_equiv: kill two birds with one stone

explain_en: It is smaller than a '강' or '개울', and a '도랑' is often a narrow channel dug to bring in or drain water. In cities people say '하수구' more, while '도랑' shows up in countryside stories.

examples.en: The children are building a sand castle on the beach.
A wave came and the sand castle collapsed.
Shall we build a sand castle together?

examples.ko: 기초가 약한 계획은 모래성처럼 금방 무너져요.
examples.en: A plan with a weak foundation collapses quickly like a sand castle.
I stuck a small flag on top of the sand castle.

examples.ko: 모래성에 물을 조금 부으면 더 단단해져요.
examples.en: If you pour a little water on the sand castle, it gets firmer.

explain: 모래성은 '쌓다, 만들다'와 함께 쓰고, 무너질 때는 '무너지다', 일부러 부술 때는 '허물다'를 써요. 기초가 약해서 쉽게 무너질 것을 비유할 때도 '모래성'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I built a sand castle with my child.
phrases.nuance_ko: '쌓다'와 비슷하게 만든다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '쌓다', meaning to build one.

phrases.example: 동생이 제 모래성을 허물어서 화가 났어요.
phrases.en: I got angry because my little brother knocked down my sand castle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일부러 부술 때 '허물다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '허물다' is used when knocking something down on purpose.

phrases.en: That plan is like a sand castle, so I feel uneasy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기초가 약해 쉽게 무너질 일을 비유해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A metaphor for something weak that could easily collapse.

explain_en: Use '쌓다' or '만들다' for building one, '무너지다' when it collapses, and '허물다' when you tear it down on purpose. '모래성' is also used figuratively for something so poorly founded that it falls apart easily.

examples.en: The hen lays eggs every morning.

examples.ko: 암탉 한 마리가 병아리들을 데리고 다녀요.
examples.en: A hen is walking around with her chicks.
They raise hens at my grandmother's house in the countryside.
I learned how to tell hens and roosters apart.
A hen is pecking at feed in the yard.

examples.ko: 이 암탉은 알을 품고 있어서 예민해요.
examples.en: This hen is sitting on her eggs, so she is touchy.

explain: 암컷 닭을 말하고, 수컷은 '수탉'이라고 해요. '탉'의 받침 ㄺ이 [ㄱ]으로 소리 나서 [암탁], [수탁]으로 읽어요. '닭'은 암수를 구별하지 않을 때 쓰는 말이에요.

phrases.en: A hen and a rooster are together in the yard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 암컷과 수컷 닭을 함께 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A paired phrase used when talking about female and male chickens together.

phrases.example: 알을 품은 암탉이 가만히 앉아 있어요.
phrases.en: The hen sitting on her eggs stays still.
phrases.nuance_ko: '암탉'이 하는 행동을 설명하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes what a hen does, sitting on eggs to keep them warm.

phrases.example: 닭장 안에 암탉이 열 마리 있어요.
phrases.en: There are ten hens in the chicken coop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 암탉이 사는 장소와 함께 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say where the hens live.

explain_en: It means a female chicken, and the male is '수탉'. The final cluster ㄺ in '탉' sounds like ㄱ, so they are pronounced [암탁] and [수탁]. '닭' is the general word when you don't distinguish sex.

examples.en: Milk should be stored at a low temperature.
I put the fruit in a cold storage room.
Low-temperature burns happen without you noticing.
You bake this dish slowly at a low temperature.
Batteries drain quickly in low temperatures.
I bought low-temperature pasteurized milk.

explain: 반대말은 '고온'이에요. 날씨는 '춥다', '쌀쌀하다'로 말하고, '저온'은 보관·요리·과학처럼 온도를 따질 때 주로 써요. '저온 보관', '저온 창고', '저온 화상'처럼 합쳐서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: Meat has to be kept at a low temperature.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식이나 물건을 낮은 온도에 두는 것을 말할 때 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for keeping food or goods at a low temperature.

phrases.en: I baked the bread slowly at a low temperature.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리할 때 낮은 온도를 말하려고 '저온에서'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In cooking, 저온에서 means at a low temperature.

phrases.en: This milk was pasteurized at a low temperature.
phrases.nuance_ko: 우유나 주스 포장에서 자주 보는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase you often see on milk and juice packages.

explain_en: The opposite is '고온'. For weather people say '춥다' or '쌀쌀하다', and '저온' is mainly used when temperature matters, as in storage, cooking and science. It often appears in compounds like '저온 보관', '저온 창고' and '저온 화상'.

examples.ko: 이불에 진드기가 생기지 않게 자주 빨아요.
examples.en: I wash my blanket often so mites don't develop.
I got bitten by a tick in the mountains and went to the hospital.
House dust mites cause allergies.
I removed a tick from the puppy's body.
I sprayed mite repellent.
Mites are almost invisible to the eye.

explain: '진드기'는 아주 작은 벌레로 이불이나 반려동물, 풀숲에서 피를 빠는 종류도 있어요. 한국에서 '진드기에 물리다'는 야외 활동 뒤에 주의하라는 뉴스에서 자주 나와요. '벼룩'은 뛰어다니는 다른 벌레예요.

phrases.en: My nose itches because of dust mites.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집 안 먼지에 사는 진드기로, 알레르기 이야기에서 많이 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Mites that live in house dust, often mentioned in talk about allergies.

phrases.example: 뜨거운 물로 빨면 진드기를 없앨 수 있어요.
phrases.en: If you wash with hot water, you can get rid of mites.
phrases.nuance_ko: 벌레를 없앤다는 뜻으로 '없애다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 없애다 to mean getting rid of pests.

phrases.en: I put tick medicine on my puppy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 진드기를 막거나 없애는 약을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Medicine that prevents or kills mites or ticks.

explain_en: 진드기 is a very small bug, and some kinds live in blankets, on pets or in grass and suck blood. In Korea, 진드기에 물리다 often appears in news warning people to be careful after outdoor activities. 벼룩 (fleas) are different bugs that jump around.
